title: 'Zero-Topping Noodles' Gaining Popularity in Japan
paragraphs: Ramen is one of the most popular foods in all of Japan. A bowl of ramen usually comes with toppings such as sliced pork, a boiled egg and bamboo shoots. But recently, ramen with no toppings at all has been gaining attention.
This very simple style of ramen contains only the noodles and the soup. Some people call it "zero-topping" ramen.

One reason for the trend is rising costs. The prices of many ingredients have gone up, so ramen shops need to charge more. However, many shops are afraid to go over the "1,000-yen wall." This is the idea that customers will stop coming if a bowl of ramen costs more than 1,000 yen.
Selling ramen without toppings is one way to solve this problem. Shops can raise the price of their regular ramen, while still offering a cheaper choice for customers who want to save money.

For example, a shop called MAIKAGURA in Setagaya, Tokyo, sells a bowl of noodles and soup with no toppings for 880 yen. Its regular ramen, with pork, egg and bamboo shoots, costs about 1,180 yen. The shop's owner said that sales of the cheaper bowl have grown as prices in Japan have gone up. A chain called Gyoza no Manchu also sells soy sauce ramen without pork for 400 yen.
Zero-topping ramen can also be found at convenience stores. In recent years, some cup noodle products have been sold with only noodles and soup.

Not everyone is happy about the trend, however. Some people online say it is a sign that Japan is becoming poorer. But others like having a cheaper choice, and some enjoy the freedom to decide for themselves which toppings, if any, to add.
